rule_metadata.rule_name_english: Tafkheem & Tarqeeq (Heavy and Light Letters & Detailed Rules of Ra)
rule_metadata.description: The definitive master module for Tafkheem (velarization/heaviness) and Tarqeeq (attenuation/lightness), including the 3 letter categories and exhaustive conditional rules for the letter Ra.

definitions.tafkheem: Tafkheem (تَفْخِيم): Heaviness or velarization—producing a full, echoing resonance in the mouth by elevating the back of the tongue toward the soft palate.
definitions.tarqeeq: Tarqeeq (تَرْقِيق): Lightness or attenuation—producing a thin, flat resonance by keeping the tongue lowered away from the soft palate.

three_letter_categories.permanently_heavy: 1. Permanently Heavy (7 Isti'la' letters): خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ (خ، ص، ض، غ، ط، ق، ظ). Always read with Tafkheem.
three_letter_categories.conditionally_heavy_or_light: 2. Conditionally Heavy or Light (3 letters): Alif Madd (follows the weight of preceding letter), Lam of Jalalah (heavy after Fathah/Dammah, light after Kasrah), and Ra (ر).
three_letter_categories.permanently_light: 3. Permanently Light (21 Istifal letters): All remaining letters of the Arabic alphabet.

ra_tafkheem_heavy: 1. When carrying a Fathah or Dammah (e.g., رَبَّنَا, رُحَمَاء).
2. When Saakinah preceded by a Fathah or Dammah (e.g., مَرْحَمَة, قُرْآن).
3. When Saakinah due to Waqf preceded by a Saakin letter which is preceded by Fathah or Dammah (e.g., وَالْعَصْر, خُسْر).
4. When Saakinah preceded by an temporary/connecting Hamzah (Hamzat al-Wasl) (e.g., ارْجِعِي).
5. When Saakinah preceded by a Kasrah but followed by an Isti'la' letter carrying a Fathah in the same word (e.g., قِرْطَاس, مِرْصَاد).
ra_tarqeeq_light: 2. When Saakinah preceded by an original Kasrah in the same word, NOT followed by an Isti'la' letter (e.g., فِرْعَوْن).
3. When Saakinah due to Waqf preceded by Ya Saakinah (Lin or Madd) (e.g., خَيْر, قَدِير).
4. When Saakinah due to Waqf preceded by a non-Isti'la' Saakin letter which is preceded by a Kasrah (e.g., حِجْر).
ra_permissible_either_way: 1. When Saakinah preceded by Kasrah and followed by an Isti'la' letter carrying Kasrah: فِرْقٍ in Surah Ash-Shu'ara.
2. When stopping (Waqf) on words with a dropped original Ya: كَنُذُر, يَسْر, and the words عِمْصْر, الْقِطْر.

practical_examples.breakdown: The 7 letters of Isti'la' that are always pronounced with full Tafkheem.
Ra Saakinah preceded by Kasrah, but followed by heavy Saad carrying Fathah.
Ra Saakinah preceded by genuine original Kasrah inside the same word.
Ra Saakinah preceded by Kasrah and followed by heavy Qaf carrying Kasrah.

assessment_bank.question: What does 'Tafkheem' mean in Tajweed?
options: Heaviness or velarization producing a full-mouth resonance

assessment_bank.question: What does 'Tarqeeq' mean in Tajweed?
options: Lightness or attenuation producing a thin resonance

assessment_bank.question: How many letters of the Arabic alphabet are PERMANENTLY heavy?
Which 3 letters in Arabic are conditionally heavy or light based on context?
options: Alif Madd, Lam of Jalalah, and Ra (ر)

assessment_bank.question: How does Alif Madd determine its weight (Tafkheem vs. Tarqeeq)?
options: It mirrors the weight of the letter immediately preceding it
It depends on the succeeding letter

assessment_bank.question: When is the letter Ra (ر) pronounced heavy due to its own vowel?
options: When it carries a Fathah or Dammah
When it is preceded by Ya

assessment_bank.question: When is the letter Ra (ر) pronounced light due to its own vowel?
options: When it carries a Kasrah (e.g., رِجَال)

assessment_bank.question: In 'مَرْحَمَة', why is the Ra Saakinah heavy?
options: Because it is preceded by a Fathah on Meem
Because it is followed by Ya

assessment_bank.question: In 'فِرْعَوْن', why is the Ra Saakinah light?
options: Because it is preceded by an original Kasrah in the same word without an Isti'la' letter following
Because it is preceded by Fathah

assessment_bank.question: In 'مِرْصَادًا', why is the Ra Saakinah heavy despite being preceded by a Kasrah?
options: Because it is immediately followed by an Isti'la' letter (Saad) carrying a Fathah in the same word

assessment_bank.question: In 'ارْجِعِي', why is the Ra Saakinah heavy?
options: Because it is preceded by a temporary connecting Hamzah (Hamzat al-Wasl)

assessment_bank.question: When stopping (Waqf) on 'خَيْر', how is the Ra pronounced?
options: Light (Tarqeeq) because it is preceded by a Ya Saakinah

assessment_bank.question: In 'كُلُّ فِرْقٍ', what is the rule regarding the Ra?
options: Permissible either way (Jawaz al-Wajhayn) because the following Isti'la' letter carries Kasrah

assessment_bank.question: In 'وَالْعَصْر', when stopping at the verse end, how is the Ra pronounced?
options: Heavy (Tafkheem) because the letter before Saad has a Fathah

assessment_bank.question: In 'حِجْر', when stopping at the verse end, how is the Ra pronounced?
options: Light (Tarqeeq) because the letter before Jeem has a Kasrah

assessment_bank.question: How many levels of Tafkheem exist for Isti'la' letters according to Ibn al-Jazari?
Which level of Tafkheem is the strongest?
options: An Isti'la' letter carrying a Fathah followed by an Alif (e.g., قَالَ)

assessment_bank.question: Which level of Tafkheem is the weakest (Tafkheem Nisbi)?
options: An Isti'la' letter carrying a Kasrah (e.g., قِيلَ)

assessment_bank.question: If a student pronounces 'فِرْعَوْن' with a heavy full-mouth Ra, what error is flagged?
options: Incorrect Tafkheem on a Ra that requires Tarqeeq (lightness after Kasrah)

assessment_bank.question: What is the primary pedagogical goal of the Tafkheem & Tarqeeq module?
options: Mastering heavy vs. light letter categories and all conditional rules governing the letter Ra

assessment_bank.question: In 'قِرْطَاس', why is the Ra heavy?
options: Followed by heavy Tah with Fathah in the same word

assessment_bank.question: In 'رُحَمَاء', why is the Ra heavy?
In 'قَدِير', when stopping (Waqf), why is the Ra light?
What happens to the letter Ra when stopping on 'مِصْر'?
options: Permissible either way (Jawaz al-Wajhayn), with heavy being preferred by many scholars

assessment_bank.question: What happens to the letter Ra when stopping on 'الْقِطْر'?
options: Permissible either way (Jawaz al-Wajhayn), with light being preferred by many scholars

assessment_bank.question: Are the letters of Itbaq (ص، ض، ط، ظ) heavier than non-Itbaq Isti'la' letters (خ، غ، ق)?
options: Yes, Itbaq letters maintain stronger heaviness across all vowels

assessment_bank.question: In 'قَالُوا', why is the Alif Madd heavy?
options: Because it is preceded by the heavy Isti'la' letter Qaf

assessment_bank.question: In 'بِمَا', why is the Alif Madd light?
options: Because it is preceded by the light Istifal letter Baa

assessment_bank.question: In 'أَمِ ارْتَابُوا', why is the Ra Saakinah heavy?
options: Preceded by a temporary Kasrah due to Hamzat al-Wasl transition

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the core rules of Tafkheem & Tarqeeq:
options: 7 letters are permanently heavy, 21 are permanently light, while Alif, Lam Jalalah, and Ra are conditional—with Ra's weight determined by its vowel, preceding vowels, or succeeding heavy letters

assessment_bank.question: In 'الرَّحْمَٰن', why is the Ra heavy?
In 'فَرِيق', why is the Ra light?
In 'قُرْآن', why is the Ra heavy?
options: Saakinah preceded by Dammah on Qaf

assessment_bank.question: What is the physical tongue position for Tarqeeq?
options: Tongue stays lowered and flat without raising the back
Back of tongue elevated to roof of mouth

assessment_bank.question: What is the physical tongue position for Tafkheem?
options: Back of tongue elevated toward soft palate creating full mouth resonance

assessment_bank.question: In 'وَنُذُر', when stopping (Waqf), why is Ra permissible either way?
options: Due to the omission of an original ending Ya in Quranic orthography

assessment_bank.question: If a student recites 'رِجَال' with a heavy Ra, what feedback is given?
options: Apply Tarqeeq (lightness) since Ra carries a direct Kasrah

assessment_bank.question: How does an AI voice evaluation engine assess Tafkheem accuracy?
options: Detect lower formants and full acoustic resonance characteristic of back-tongue elevation

assessment_bank.question: How many conditions make the letter Ra light (Tarqeeq)?
options: 4 core conditions (Kasrah vowel, Saakin after original Kasrah, Saakin after Ya, Saakin after non-Isti'la' after Kasrah)

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the complete Tafkheem & Tarqeeq master module:
options: A comprehensive 40-question module governing heavy vs. light letter classification and all rules of Ra across heavy, light, and dual-permissible conditions
